articles.headline: Beyond the ban: Why prohibition fails to stop hooch deaths
articles.blurb: Despite stringent prohibition laws in dry states, illicit liquor continues to claim lives across India; Satish Jha and Sumir Karmakar report that a Supreme Court judgment has observed total bans have failed to curb black-market toxic brews, fuelling debate on enforcement and illegal supply chains.

articles.headline: The Left's generational divide: Young leaders, old guard
articles.blurb: Young Left leaders pushing social justice face parent parties battling electoral decline and rigid leadership, as student protests such as AISA demonstrations in Patna over electoral roll revision highlight the gap between grassroots activism and ageing party structures.

articles.headline: A bitter harvest: Ginger's fading fortunes in Karnataka
articles.blurb: Arjun Kumar Muralimath reports ginger cultivation in Karnataka is shrinking, with projected area falling to about 19,000 hectares in 2026-27 from higher recent levels, as farmers grapple with falling prices and uncertain returns despite lakhs of tonnes of production.

articles.headline: Advani hospitalised, condition stable
articles.blurb: Former deputy prime minister L K Advani was admitted to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital; his condition is reported stable.

articles.headline: Dipke released on bail; Neha Bora let off
articles.blurb: Activist Abhijeet Dipke and AISA president Neha Bora were released after detention linked to protests in the capital.

articles.headline: 2 oil tankers hit Hormuz mines
articles.blurb: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz amid heightened regional tensions.

articles.headline: Protests across France over rising costs
articles.blurb: Demonstrations spread across France over living costs, echoing past 'yellow vest' unrest as households face price pressures.

articles.headline: FSSAI notices to Hindustan Unilever, Nestle
articles.blurb: The food regulator issued notices to Hindustan Unilever and Nestle over alleged misleading claims on products including Horlicks Women's Plus and selected Nestle lines.

articles.headline: Drought grips entire state; gloomy forecast spells doomsday
articles.blurb: Sujay B M reports 226 of 240 taluks are drought-affected with estimated crop loss exceeding ₹60,000 crore, surpassing the ₹35,162 crore loss in 2023-24, as a CM-led team plans to meet the Prime Minister seeking central relief.

articles.headline: Stir against SIR; Over 45 detained
articles.blurb: Police detained over 45 AISA protesters at Bengaluru Town Hall during a stir against SIR and alleged police brutality in Delhi; a few suffered bruises as officers dragged them away after denying permission citing a High Court order restricting protests to Freedom Park.

articles.headline: Trump waives tariffs on buyers of Russian oil & gas
articles.blurb: President Donald Trump waived sanctions on goods from major purchasers of Russian oil and gas citing US national interest; India among the biggest buyers, and industry voices including FICCI welcomed relief for energy security while critics such as Senator Richard Blumenthal attacked the move.

articles.headline: Joint A-ekhata owners can subdivide plots
articles.blurb: The Greater Bengaluru Authority launched a service on e-Aasthi 2.0 allowing joint owners under a single A-ekhata to subdivide plots, with applications via https://e-Aasthi.karnataka.gov.in and helpline 9480683695.

articles.headline: Children have fundamental right to access internet: SC
articles.blurb: The Supreme Court held children have a fundamental right to access and use the internet under Article 21 and directed the Centre to create a national database to help detect sexually explicit visual content involving minors.

articles.headline: 17 killed in stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja pandal
articles.blurb: At least 17 people died and about 20 were injured in a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in central Kolkata; Union Home Minister Amit Shah visited the site.

articles.headline: CM-Siddu meeting
articles.blurb: A closed-door meeting between Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and former minister Siddu Savadi in Mysuru triggered political buzz in the state.

articles.headline: 30% cap on margins on 137 cancer drugs
articles.blurb: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority capped trade margins at 30% on 137 non-scheduled cancer drug formulations.

articles.headline: Coordination is key
articles.blurb: An Insight package on illicit liquor cites recent hooch tragedies across states, NCRB-trend data showing hundreds of spurious-liquor deaths annually, and a September 2024 Supreme Court call for multi-department coordination to curb tragedies linked to methanol adulteration.

articles.headline: Liquor prohibition, an old policy debate
articles.blurb: The sidebar traces prohibition from US history to Indian dry states such as Gujarat and Bihar, arguing bans often shift consumption to unsafe illicit markets.

articles.headline: Ideals in opposition, contradictions in power
articles.blurb: N K Bhoopesh examines how Left parties balance ideological ideals with governance, from West Bengal industrialisation conflicts to Kerala's centralised leadership and challenges of caste and identity politics. (Opinion)

articles.headline: Old kitchens await repairs, renovations in schools
articles.blurb: Naina J A reports many Dakshina Kannada school kitchens serving Akshara Dasoha midday meals to 1.37 lakh students in 1,312 schools are dilapidated or lack space, while workers' association leaders demand renovation grants stalled since 2012 and timely honorarium payments.

articles.headline: Climate-resilient research must reach farmers: MP
articles.blurb: MP Kota Srinivas Poojary told the Zonal Agricultural and Horticultural Research Station in Brahmavar that climate-resilient research must reach farmers and government schemes need sharper implementation, noting over 100 paddy varieties on display and a proposed agricultural college for the region.

articles.headline: Minimum Wages Board chief seeks panels for youth, senior citizens
articles.blurb: Karnataka State Minimum Wages Advisory Board chairman T M Shahid urged advisory panels for youth and senior citizens and said he would seek GST exemption on wages of outsourced workers.

articles.headline: 11th edition of tiger dance competition on October 20; nine teams to contest
articles.blurb: Pili Nalike Prathishthana will host the 11th 'Pili Nalike' tiger dance competition at Karavali Utsav Ground in Mangaluru on October 20 with nine invited teams competing for cash prizes.

articles.headline: Panaje records 167 mm rainfall
articles.blurb: Heavy rain lashed Dakshina Kannada with Panaje recording 167 mm; Belthangady and Mangaluru also saw significant rainfall as IMD forecast more showers for three days from a cyclonic circulation over the Arabian Sea.

articles.headline: MRPL blast: 1 more dies of injuries
articles.blurb: Contract employee Rajesh A D'Silva died of injuries from the September 28 blast at Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited, raising the toll from the incident.

articles.headline: Login ID misused for illegal ration card applications; 3 booked
articles.blurb: Mallikarjun Jalihar reports police booked three people after a food department login ID was misused to submit over 1,000 illegal applications for ration cards and other services in Yadgir.

articles.headline: Be willing to listen to others' perspectives: CJI to NLSIU grads
articles.blurb: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant told National Law School of India University graduates at its 34th annual convocation to remain open to others' perspectives.

articles.headline: HDK seeks sting op mastermind's arrest, demands SIT probe
articles.blurb: Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy filed a complaint with the DGP demanding an SIT probe into a viral sting video featuring him, alleging a political plot behind it.

articles.headline: Tension grips Nrupatunga Road
articles.blurb: Hundreds of JD(S) workers gathered outside the DG&IGP office on Nrupatunga Road as Kumaraswamy submitted his complaint, prompting police action to control the crowd.

articles.headline: Sting op video: No leads yet; cops launch tech analysis
articles.blurb: Bengaluru police are conducting technical analysis of the viral sting video to trace its source and circulation, with no major breakthrough on identities so far.

articles.headline: Centre must take soft stand on sugarcane farmers' demands: CM
articles.blurb: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah in Belagavi urged the Union government to adopt a softer approach to sugarcane growers' demands including on fair and remunerative price.

articles.headline: Modi 'father of sting ops': Hariprasad
articles.blurb: Congress leader B K Hariprasad in Gadag accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP of weaponising sting operations politically.

articles.headline: Sting op must be probed thoroughly: Vijayendra
articles.blurb: BJP state president B Y Vijayendra in Chitradurga demanded a thorough probe into the sting controversy while also referring to sugarcane farmers' issues.

articles.headline: Priyank dares HDK to prove 'Kharge's meeting with PM' claim
articles.blurb: ITBT Minister Priyank Kharge in Kalaburagi challenged Kumaraswamy to produce evidence for his claim that AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge met Prime Minister Modi.

articles.headline: Sowmya quits as Mahila Cong chief
articles.blurb: Former Jayanagar MLA Sowmya Reddy resigned as Karnataka Mahila Congress president.

articles.headline: FDA, typist of special AC office in Lokayukta net
articles.blurb: Lokayukta police caught a first division assistant and typist from a special assistant commissioner's office in Tumakuru for allegedly accepting ₹60,000 bribe to pass a favourable order.

articles.headline: Man travels 300 km to donate rare Bombay blood to save three-year-old
articles.blurb: Mahesh Kumar from Chikmagalur travelled to Dharwad to donate rare Bombay O group blood for a three-year-old boy with a rare blood disorder.

articles.headline: Long hours, no weekly offs: Surat textile workers push back
articles.blurb: Satish Jha reports Surat textile workers are demanding a weekly off and shorter shifts, clashing with owners citing rising costs; police arrested union leaders during the standoff in India's largest textile hub.

articles.headline: Relief to India as Trump waives Russia sanctions
articles.blurb: New Delhi expects to continue importing Russian crude after President Trump waived sanctions under the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia Act, with FICCI and industry voices citing relief for refiners and energy security.

articles.headline: India slams UN report, says CJP protest evidence of free speech
articles.blurb: India rejected UN Special Rapporteur Gina Romero's findings on protest retaliation, arguing demonstrations such as those against the CEC show constitutional free speech, not stigmatisation.

articles.headline: Dipke gets conditional bail, asked to sign peace bond
articles.blurb: Police released Abhijeet Dipke and AISA chief Neha Bora on conditional bail after detention during a Connaught Place protest, requiring them to sign a peace bond.

articles.headline: LK Advani admitted to hospital with chest infection
articles.blurb: Veteran BJP leader L K Advani, 98, was admitted to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital ICU with a chest infection; doctors said his condition is stable.

articles.headline: Uddhav backs regime change if voting, protest rights are curbed
articles.blurb: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray in Mumbai said he would back regime change if democratic rights to vote and protest are curtailed.

articles.headline: DMK rules out joining 'backstabber' Cong
articles.blurb: The DMK in Chennai passed a resolution ruling out alliance with the Congress it labelled a backstabber and demanding the chief election commissioner's removal while questioning EVMs.

articles.headline: 'Thenisai Thendral' Deva: Maestro took gaana to masses
articles.blurb: Composer Deva, 73, who popularised gaana music in Tamil cinema over four decades, died; tributes hailed him as 'Thenisai Thendral'.

articles.headline: Food regulator proposes ban on added sugars in foods for infants under six months
articles.blurb: FSSAI proposed banning added sucrose and fructose in infant foods up to six months to limit early sugar exposure, inviting public comments for 60 days.

articles.headline: Trump's mid-term poll setback may matter less to India
articles.blurb: Sumit Ganguly argues US midterm elections on November 2 may not sharply alter India policy because foreign affairs remain largely presidential and bipartisan support for the partnership endures. (Opinion)

articles.headline: Protests over living costs turn violent across France
articles.blurb: Nationwide French protests over living costs and student grievances turned violent with fires in Paris and Lyon; police used tear gas and water cannons as President Macron defended the right to protest while condemning property damage.

articles.headline: Israeli settlers attack European diplomatic cars, beat French mayor
articles.blurb: Israeli settlers attacked a convoy of European diplomats and assaulted a visiting French mayor during a Palestinian olive harvest in the occupied West Bank.

articles.headline: Indian seafarers safe as drone-hit tanker reaches Romanian port
articles.blurb: A chemical tanker with nine Indian crew hit by a drone off Romania reached Constanta; the Indian embassy confirmed all seafarers are safe.

articles.headline: Bangladesh's seaside resort fire claims 10 lives; Reports
articles.blurb: A fire at a Cox's Bazar seaside resort killed 10 people, including six from one family.

articles.headline: 4 new Ebola cases in Kenya
articles.blurb: Kenya confirmed four new Ebola cases, taking the national total to seven.

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital after lung surgery
articles.blurb: Pope Leo XIV left Rome's Gemelli University Hospital four days after surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung.

articles.headline: Women's golf STRUGGLING for EXPANSION
articles.blurb: Sidney Kiran writes that despite stars such as Aditi Ashok and Pranavi Urs, women's golf in India remains elite-club bound because of high equipment and coaching costs and scarce public ranges, calling for wider access.

articles.headline: Supreme Haaland stars in City victory
articles.blurb: Erling Haaland scored twice as Manchester City won in the Premier League; Liverpool beat Brentford and Chelsea defeated Everton on the same matchday.

articles.headline: Bopanna misses out on AITA's SOM roster
articles.blurb: Rohan Bopanna was left off the All India Tennis Association Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit list for not meeting the mandatory one-year retirement criterion.

articles.headline: Relentless Fokina slays Zverev
articles.blurb: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina beat Alexander Zverev in straight sets at the Shanghai Masters.

articles.headline: Chacarra surges to two-shot lead
articles.blurb: Spain's Eugenio Chacarra led by two shots when the DP World Tour third round in New Delhi was halted for bad light.

articles.headline: Kartal in final
articles.blurb: Sonay Kartal reached a WTA 1000 final.

articles.headline: Atletico scrape past Espanyol
articles.blurb: Atletico Madrid beat Espanyol 1-0 with a late goal in Cornella de Llobregat.

articles.headline: Torobravo wins Rani Rudrama Devi Trophy
articles.blurb: Hyderabad race results listed Torobravo among winners of the Rani Rudrama Devi Trophy meeting along with dividends for seven races.

articles.headline: Lady Scarlet for feature
articles.blurb: Pune race selections tipped Lady Scarlet for the feature event.

articles.headline: Asiad Para: Manasi, Thulasimita assure India medal
articles.blurb: At the Asian Para Games in Nagoya, Manasi Joshi and Thulasimathi Murugesan secured badminton medals while Bhavina Patel extended her table-tennis winning run and India's blind football team lost to Japan.

articles.headline: Rain has final say in decider
articles.blurb: The fifth India–West Indies T20I at Bengaluru's Chinnaswamy Stadium was abandoned in rain after India reached 118/5 in 7.4 overs with Ishan Kishan making 38 off 10 balls, leaving the series shared 2-2.

articles.headline: K'taka's Puneeth completes golden double
articles.blurb: Karnataka's Puneeth Manoharan won boys' under-14 singles and doubles at the Junior National Open Tennis Championship in New Delhi, beating Satya Prakash of Telangana in the singles final.

articles.headline: Amruta takes silver as Indian women finish with two medals
articles.blurb: Amruta won silver in women's 72kg at the U-23 World Wrestling Championships in Las Vegas, losing the final to Ukraine's Iryna Zablotska as India finished with two women's medals.

articles.headline: India's top-order eyes improved show
articles.blurb: After winning the first women's T20I against Zimbabwe, India targets a series lead in Raipur with debutant Niki Prasad in focus.

articles.headline: IPL auction in Goa on Dec 16
articles.blurb: BCCI set the IPL player auction for the 2027 season on December 16 in Goa.

articles.headline: Mahela quits MI, Vaas joins Capitals
articles.blurb: Mahela Jayawardene stepped down as Mumbai Indians head coach while Chaminda Vaas joined Delhi Capitals as fast bowling coach.

articles.headline: BUDAA meet on Oct 26 & 27
articles.blurb: Bangalore Urban District Athletic Association will hold its meet at Sree Kanteerava Stadium on October 26 and 27.

articles.headline: Karnataka need batting reset
articles.blurb: Vignesh Bharadwaj previews Karnataka's Ranji Trophy opener against Saurashtra under Shreyas Gopal, saying top-order batters including Mayank Agarwal and Devdutt Padikkal must find form.

articles.headline: Williams, Perovic on target as BFC slay Chennaiyin
articles.blurb: Bengaluru FC beat Chennaiyin FC 2-0 in the Indian Super League with goals from Ryan Williams and Milos Perovic.

articles.headline: Ashwin for playing 4 frontline seamers in NZ Tests
articles.blurb: R Ashwin said India should consider four specialist fast bowlers for the New Zealand Test series to suit local conditions.

articles.headline: Poison for some, medicine for others (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Aakash Singh Rathore uses Derrida's 'Plato's Pharmacy' to discuss campus reading-list controversies targeting Ambedkar, Periyar and Phule, asking whether knowledge acts as cure or poison.

articles.headline: There is anger in the air (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Harish Bijoor argues prime-time TV and social media have normalised public rage, shaping how people argue and consume news.

articles.headline: Profiles in cowardice (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Roger Marshall critiques political and tech leaders including Donald Trump, Joe Biden and Mark Zuckerberg for failing moral courage amid democratic and technological risks.

articles.headline: Dead novel in its afterlife (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Sumana Roy reflects on Milan Kundera's idea of the 'dead novel' and how postcolonial writing challenges Western literary canons.

articles.headline: The verdict-first dissent: India's politics of negation (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Gurucharan Gollerkeri contends Indian parties increasingly reject institutional outcomes such as election commission or court decisions before they are rendered, eroding democratic trust.

articles.headline: The business of becoming better
articles.blurb: Prachi Srivastava examines the self-improvement industry's promise of fitness, calm and productivity, asking who profits from perpetual dissatisfaction and whether empowerment has become exploitation.

articles.headline: London's very own 'Bangalore Street'
articles.blurb: Stanley Carvalho describes Putney's Victorian-era Bangalore Street in south-west London, named when empire-era soldiers returned from Bangalore.

articles.headline: Living by the (QR) code
articles.blurb: M S Sriram reviews Santanu Paul and B Sambamurthy's Cashless Nation (Penguin, ₹599) on how NPCI and partners built UPI into a global digital payments model.

articles.headline: Myth and reality in a troubled land
articles.blurb: Sudipta Datta reviews Lian Dousel's Peace in the Land of the Dead (Hachette, ₹599), short fiction on conflict and identity in Manipur.

articles.headline: Mood board: October comfort reads
articles.blurb: The books desk recommends Gabrielle Zevin's The Storied Life of A J Fikry, Ann Patchett's The Dutch House and Sangu Mandanna's The Very Secret Society of Irregular Witches as warm autumn reads.

articles.headline: Are there enough ladders to climb?
articles.blurb: Srinath Sridharan reviews Anirudh Krishna's Why Kenyans Win Marathons and Estonians Build Unicorns (Penguin, ₹599) on how opportunity structures—not mystery talent—produce excellence.

articles.headline: Read of the week: The Assault on Truth
articles.blurb: The column highlights Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson's book challenging Freud's retraction of his early seduction theory on childhood trauma.

articles.headline: In the court of Public Opinion
articles.blurb: Sumit Singla discusses how a Delhi Metro reader filmed without consent while reading a thriller was judged online, linking surveillance culture to gendered readings of crime stories.

articles.headline: DECODED: The art of DRAG
articles.blurb: The piece traces drag's role in LGBTQIA+ performance and political commentary, citing artists such as Sick, Maya the Drag Queen and Patruni Sastry.

articles.headline: WHEN A CITY speaks
articles.blurb: Kiran Mehta explores Sydney through sound—from didgeridoo players at the Opera House to kookaburras, kangaroos at Emerald Beach and Hay Street Market bustle.

articles.headline: Odisha on a platter
articles.blurb: Sandip Das, Alka Jena and Pallavi Das survey Odia cuisine from Jagannath temple abadha to tribal and coastal dishes including pakhala, chakuli pitha and manda pitha.

articles.headline: THE OBBATTU: A layered history
articles.blurb: Savitha Karthik traces obbattu or holige from medieval texts such as Manasollasa through regional sweet and savoury fillings.

articles.headline: Uneven burden of pain
articles.blurb: Dr Raghavendra Ramanujulu cites a Nature Medicine study across 204 countries showing women report more bodily pain than men, especially before age 55, urging clinicians to listen differently.

articles.headline: Your guide to fibromyalgia
articles.blurb: Savitha Karthik's Take Five explains fibromyalgia symptoms, diagnosis without a single test, lack of permanent cure and lifestyle measures that can help manage pain and fatigue.

articles.headline: The many facets of remembrance
articles.blurb: Neha Kirpal profiles Asit Kumar Patnaik's Bikaner House solo show curated by Shibani Chawla, where women drawn from Banaras memories anchor his colourful figurative work.

articles.headline: When the body becomes a temple
articles.blurb: Souvik Ghosh describes how Chhattisgarh's Ramnami Samaj, who tattoo Ram's name as anti-caste devotion, inspired Maniktala Chaltabagan Lohapatty Durga Puja in Kolkata.

articles.headline: Traditional flavours for every occasion
articles.blurb: DH Brandspot shares recipes for masala vade and kayi sasive anna as part of an LG Cooking Secrets feature on festive Karnataka dishes.
